entry.title: Greg Slepak publishes short leash AI coding method to improve performance on Fable, July 2026
entry.summary: Greg Slepak has introduced a new AI coding technique called the "short leash" method, aimed at enhancing performance in the Fable programming environment. This approach focuses on improving the efficiency and effectiveness of AI-driven code generation and execution. The method was detailed in a blog post published in July 2026, where Slepak explains the principles behind the technique and its potential benefits for developers working with AI-assisted coding tools. Early discussions and feedback from the programming community highlight its promise in optimizing AI interactions within software development.

entry.title: claude-real-video enables any large language model to analyze videos locally by extracting key frames, transcribing audio, and generating readable manifests without uploading data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: claude-real-video is a tool that enables large language models (LLMs) like Claude to analyze videos locally by extracting key frames based on scene changes, transcribing audio, and generating readable manifests without uploading any data. Unlike other AI tools that sample frames at fixed intervals or rely on transcripts alone, this tool intelligently selects meaningful frames and provides a clean folder of frames, transcripts, and metadata for any LLM to process on the user's machine. The tool uses ffmpeg for frame extraction and audio processing, yt-dlp for fetching videos from URLs, and optionally Whisper for audio transcription. It supports various video sources including YouTube, Instagram, and local files, and can handle login-gated content with cookies. By focusing on scene changes and deduplicating similar frames, claude-real-video offers a more efficient and accurate way for LLMs to "watch" videos, enabling better understanding without sending data to external servers.

entry.title: Natural 20 publishes guide to building an AI chat endpoint in Node.js using the Telnyx AI Assistants API [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Natural 20 has published a guide demonstrating how to build an AI chat endpoint in Node.js using the Telnyx AI Assistants API. The guide provides developers with practical instructions to integrate AI chat capabilities into their applications through this API. This resource aims to simplify the process of creating AI-driven chat endpoints, leveraging Telnyx's platform to enhance communication functionalities in Node.js environments.

entry.title: Godot maintainers ban AI-generated code contributions and require explicit approval for new contributors amid concerns over code quality and review challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The Godot game engine maintainers have announced a new contribution policy that bans AI-generated code contributions and requires explicit approval for new contributors submitting significant changes. This decision comes after an influx of AI-generated pull requests, which the team found difficult to review and often of poor quality, leading to frustration and demoralization among maintainers. The policy aims to ensure contributors understand the codebase and engage in meaningful human-to-human communication during the review process. Under the updated guidelines, new contributors with three or fewer merged pull requests must obtain permission before submitting new features or major refactoring. The use of AI is restricted to minor tasks like code completion, and any AI-assisted code must be disclosed. Autonomous AI-generated contributions will result in an automatic ban from the project's GitHub repository. The maintainers emphasize that this approach is necessary to maintain code quality and effective collaboration within the Godot community.

entry.title: Mozilla.ai announces transcribe.cpp, an open-source C/C++ speech-to-text inference library with GPU acceleration support for multiple STT models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Mozilla.ai has released transcribe.cpp, an open-source C/C++ speech-to-text inference library that supports multiple STT models with GPU acceleration via Metal, Vulkan, and CUDA backends. The library aims to provide a uniform interface for efficient and portable speech transcription, addressing common issues of limited portability and suboptimal performance in existing models. Developed with support from Mozilla.ai's Builders in Residence program, transcribe.cpp builds on previous contributions by CJ Pais and integrates with tools like Handy and llamafile to enable easy transcription tasks and model bundling. This release offers developers a versatile resource to incorporate advanced speech-to-text capabilities into their applications while promoting open collaboration in applied AI research.

entry.title: B2B marketing agency reaches $1.5M ARR in six months by rebuilding its operating model around AI-native strategies and tools [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A B2B marketing agency transformed its business by fully integrating AI into its operating model, achieving $1.5 million in annual recurring revenue within six months. Rather than simply adding AI tools to existing workflows, the agency rebuilt its processes around AI-native strategies, including Answer Engine Optimization and cohort-led account-based marketing, which significantly improved demand generation and client engagement. The agency's approach involved developing proprietary AI tools to automate research, segmentation, messaging, and campaign optimization, enabling a small team of experienced operators to manage a larger scope of work efficiently. This shift also led to a higher sales close rate, as prospects engaged with AI-driven content before direct contact, fostering trust early in the sales process. The agency's success highlights the importance of adopting AI as a fundamental operational structure rather than a supplementary tool.

entry.title: Alibaba bans employees from using Anthropic's Claude AI models on work devices over security concerns [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Alibaba Group has banned its employees from using Anthropic's Claude AI models on company devices due to security concerns. The company has directed staff to remove all Claude-related software from their work computers, highlighting its cautious approach to integrating external AI technologies into its operations.

entry.title: GeekyAnts explains why SSO, audit logs, and RBAC are essential for securing AI applications in production environments [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: GeekyAnts highlights the necessity of integrating Single Sign-On (SSO), audit logs, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) when transitioning AI applications from prototype stages to production environments. These features are essential for maintaining secure user access, tracking system activities, and managing permissions effectively in live AI systems. The article emphasizes that implementing these security measures helps organizations ensure accountability and protect sensitive data as AI applications scale and become integral to business operations.

entry.title: Oracle halves Always Free Ampere A1 compute limits from 4 OCPUs and 24 GB RAM to 2 OCPUs and 12 GB RAM without public announcement, causing user confusion over pay-as-you-go impact
entry.summary: Oracle has quietly reduced the Always Free Ampere A1 compute resources on its cloud platform from 4 OCPUs and 24 GB RAM to 2 OCPUs and 12 GB RAM, effective June 15, 2026, without any public announcement or direct customer notification. This change has caused confusion among users, particularly regarding whether pay-as-you-go (PAYG) accounts are affected, as official documentation states the new limits apply to all tenancies, while support agents have indicated the restrictions may only impact free-tier accounts. The reduction halves the previously generous free-tier capacity, which attracted a broad user base including developers and self-hosters. Users discovered the change when instances were unexpectedly shut down or when updated limits appeared on Oracle's website. The lack of clear communication has led to uncertainty about potential billing for PAYG users and concerns over the permanence of these new limits, especially since terminated instances may not be recreated above the reduced thresholds. This situation highlights issues with Oracle's approach to modifying free-tier offerings, as the absence of transparent communication risks eroding user trust. Affected users are advised to review their Ampere A1 instance usage to comply with the new limits and to seek confirmation from Oracle Support regarding their account status to avoid unexpected charges or service interruptions.

entry.title: Andy Masley argues AI art functions primarily as curation, enabling users to select and organize artistic elements rather than create original works, highlighting collaborative creativity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Andy Masley presents AI-generated art as a form of curation rather than traditional creation, emphasizing how users select and organize artistic elements to express specific tastes and emotions. He compares the process to assembling a playlist or arranging unique objects, highlighting the collaborative nature of human creativity and AI technology. Masley explains that while AI art may not evoke the same satisfaction as creating art by hand, it enables users to explore and communicate nuanced feelings and aesthetics that are difficult to articulate otherwise. This approach allows for a personalized experience that resonates emotionally, even if the AI itself is not the original creator. This perspective suggests that AI art expands creative possibilities by offering new ways to discover and share artistic expressions, fostering connections among people with similar tastes. It challenges traditional notions of authorship and highlights the value of curation as a distinct and meaningful creative outlet.

entry.title: UK enacts generational tobacco sales ban for those born after 2009 despite uncertainty over its effectiveness
entry.summary: The UK has enacted a generational tobacco sales ban under the Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026, prohibiting the sale of tobacco products to anyone born after January 1, 2009, indefinitely. This "endgame" policy aims to eliminate smoking entirely among future generations, marking a significant shift in tobacco control strategy. However, the effectiveness of such bans remains uncertain, as similar laws in other countries have faced challenges or repeal. The ban reflects changing social attitudes toward smoking, especially among younger people who are increasingly repulsed by the habit. While the policy targets future smokers, experts emphasize the need for comprehensive approaches that also support current smokers. The UK law has drawn international attention, potentially influencing tobacco control efforts worldwide, though political opposition and questions about long-term enforcement persist.

entry.title: Kuaishou raises $2 billion for AI video unit Kling, valuing it at $18 billion ahead of planned Hong Kong IPO [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Kuaishou has raised approximately $2 billion for its AI video division, Kling, valuing the unit at $18 billion ahead of a planned initial public offering (IPO) in Hong Kong. The funding round was led by investors including CPE, Guofang Investment, BlueFive, Tencent, and Citic Securities, with the potential to increase to $3 billion as more investors join. This move positions Kling among a growing number of Chinese AI companies preparing for IPOs in Hong Kong, reflecting the expanding interest in AI-driven video technology.

entry.title: MIT Technology Review: Companies integrate AI with Lean Six Sigma and BPM frameworks to enhance operational excellence amid a projected $113 billion AI process optimization market [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Companies are increasingly integrating artificial intelligence with established operational frameworks like Lean Six Sigma and business process management (BPM) to enhance process excellence. These traditional methodologies, known for bringing structure and clarity to complex operations through statistical rigor and workflow mapping, are evolving as AI technologies offer new opportunities for optimization. The market for AI-driven process optimization is expected to surpass $113 billion in the coming decade, with a majority of business leaders planning to boost investments in AI-enhanced process intelligence soon. Organizations with mature process disciplines are better positioned to leverage AI effectively, as they already have a culture of data-driven decision-making and process accountability. This foundation allows them to embed AI tools into proven systems rather than applying them superficially, increasing the likelihood of achieving meaningful operational improvements. The convergence of technology and process management is becoming essential for companies aiming to realize the full benefits of both AI and established process excellence frameworks.

entry.title: Alan Buxton contrasts skepticism about AI reliability with effective prompt engineering to harness AI capabilities, highlighting generational differences in AI perception and use [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Alan Buxton explores contrasting attitudes toward AI, highlighting skepticism among younger generations who often find AI unreliable, while older professionals leverage effective prompt engineering to maximize AI's usefulness. He attributes these differences to generational experiences and expectations shaped by cultural portrayals of AI and practical familiarity with its capabilities. Buxton explains that large language models serve as an average of global knowledge, which can be highly effective in well-established domains but less reliable in niche or rapidly evolving areas, such as specific gaming contexts. He notes that younger users, still exploring their place in the world, may resist AI's tendency to provide generalized answers, whereas experienced users can better discern when AI outputs are helpful or flawed. The article suggests that while older generations may overestimate AI's sentience due to cultural influences, younger users' skepticism reflects a realistic response to AI's current limitations. This generational divide underscores the evolving relationship with AI technology and the importance of understanding its strengths and weaknesses in different contexts.

entry.title: Researchers present PACE, a neuro-symbolic framework combining neural models and symbolic reasoning to generate feasible, actionable counterfactual explanations with domain constraints [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed PACE, a neuro-symbolic framework that combines neural predictive models with symbolic reasoning to generate counterfactual explanations that are both feasible and actionable within domain constraints. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods that often produce unrealistic recommendations by explicitly incorporating domain knowledge and intervention constraints during explanation generation. PACE separates prediction and reasoning into distinct components, enabling it to produce explanations that align with human-understandable rules and feasible actions while remaining interpretable and model-agnostic. The framework was demonstrated on the Adult Income dataset, where a multilayer perceptron classifier was paired with symbolic rules encoded in Answer Set Programming to enforce feasible changes to attributes like education, occupation, and working hours, while preserving immutable features. Results showed that incorporating symbolic constraints improves the plausibility and domain-specific feasibility of counterfactual explanations, highlighting a trade-off between validity and realism. This work illustrates the potential of neuro-symbolic methods to enhance transparency and practicality in explainable AI systems.

entry.title: Researchers present Auto-FL-Research, an agentic workflow for automated federated learning algorithm search, evaluated on healthcare and LEAF datasets with mixed performance outcomes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Auto-FL-Research (AFR), an automated workflow that uses agent-based search to explore algorithmic choices in federated learning (FL). AFR allows agents to propose and implement variations in training algorithms, including server aggregation, client update schedules, and model variants, while controlling for compute budget and evaluation criteria. The system was tested on healthcare-related FL tasks and standard LEAF datasets, showing improvements in several cases but also revealing sensitivity to random seeds and some failures. The evaluation involved repeated trials to distinguish genuine algorithmic improvements from tuning effects or single-run artifacts. Results indicated that some performance gains stemmed from changes in FL recipes, while others were due to fixed-surface parameter tuning or did not hold under repeated or held-out evaluations. These findings highlight the complexity of automated FL algorithm search and the importance of rigorous testing to separate robust improvements from incidental effects.

entry.title: Researchers present Wiola, a novel Small Language Model architecture with five new components, released in four sizes and compatible with HuggingFace Transformers [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Wiola, a novel Small Language Model (SLM) architecture developed independently from existing models like GPT, LLaMA, Mistral, or Falcon. Wiola features five new components, including Spiral Rotary Positional Encoding for advanced token positioning, Gated Cross-Layer Attention for enhanced layer interaction, Adaptive Token Merging to reduce attention complexity, Dual Stream Feed-Forward replacing traditional MLPs, and WiolaRMSNorm to prevent representation collapse. The model is available in four sizes ranging from 120 million to 1.5 billion parameters and is fully compatible with the HuggingFace Transformers ecosystem. The researchers provide detailed mathematical derivations, architectural diagrams, and complexity analyses, comparing Wiola systematically against established models such as GPT-2, LLaMA-2, and Mistral. All 22 architectural unit tests for Wiola have passed, demonstrating its robustness and potential for efficient language modeling.

entry.title: Researchers propose Agent4cs, a multi-agent system that improves code summarization in large hierarchical codebases by up to 38% in keyword coverage and 8% in semantic consistency [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Agent4cs, a multi-agent system designed to improve code summarization in large, hierarchical codebases. Unlike traditional methods that treat source code as flat text and rely on a single language model, Agent4cs uses a bottom-up approach with specialized agents for summarization, keyword extraction, and quality assurance. This framework enhances the understanding of complex code structures by leveraging interdependencies within repositories. Evaluations on seven advanced models show that Agent4cs increases semantic consistency by an average of 8% across folder levels compared to existing structured prompting baselines. Additionally, tests on real-world datasets demonstrate up to a 38% improvement in normalized keyword coverage, indicating more comprehensive and accurate code summaries.

entry.title: Researchers propose difficulty-routed control architecture for autonomous customer-service agents to improve operational reliability by routing complex requests to escalated workflows in retail and airline tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a difficulty-routed control architecture for autonomous customer-service agents to enhance operational reliability by directing complex service requests to escalated workflows. This approach maintains efficiency for routine tasks while applying more rigorous control to requests involving conflicts among customer instructions, policies, and backend operations, such as refunds and reservation changes. The system uses a lightweight router to distinguish between routine and operationally coupled sessions, ensuring that critical cases receive additional deliberation before backend actions are executed. The architecture was tested on human-verified retail and airline tasks, demonstrating consistent improvements in handling requests with operational conflicts. Rather than broadly increasing interaction or tool use, the escalated workflow focuses on gathering evidence, separating write operations, and reconsidering actions before execution. This method preserves fallback options, correctly associates records with actions, sequences writes appropriately, and manages multi-entity requests, extending its effectiveness from retail scenarios to airline reservation operations.

entry.title: Researchers introduce CreativityNeuro, a data-free method using contrastive weight steering to improve divergent thinking and reduce mode collapse in large language models, showing up to 14 percentile point gains on creativity tests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed CreativityNeuro, a novel data-free technique that enhances divergent thinking in large language models (LLMs) by using contrastive weight steering. This method addresses the common issue of LLMs producing similar responses to open-ended questions, known as the artificial hivemind effect, and has demonstrated improvements of up to 14 percentile points on creativity tests such as the Divergent Association Task (DAT). CreativityNeuro also showed significant gains in originality, surprise, and creativity in large-scale human evaluations on the Alternative Uses Test (AUT) and the Task Task, while effectively reducing mode collapse across these tasks. Unlike activation steering, which performed well only on the DAT, CreativityNeuro's weight-space steering generalized effectively to more complex and open-ended tasks without requiring behavioral data, retraining, or gradient-based fine-tuning. This approach offers a straightforward way to boost the creative capabilities of LLMs, potentially enhancing their performance in various creative domains.

entry.title: Researchers adapt DiffusionGemma-26B diffusion language model for interactive radiology report drafting, outperforming autoregressive models in speed and any-order text infill capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have adapted the DiffusionGemma-26B diffusion language model for interactive radiology report drafting, demonstrating that it matches or outperforms its autoregressive counterpart, Gemma-4-26B, in medical visual question answering tasks. The diffusion model offers significantly faster decoding speeds-3.5 to 4.4 times faster-and supports any-order text infill, allowing radiologists to edit report fragments and have the model fill in the gaps, a capability not available in autoregressive models. This advancement leverages the bidirectional denoising process of diffusion models, which contrasts with the left-to-right token generation of autoregressive models. The approach is particularly suited to real-world radiology reports, which often contain terse or inconsistent text across different clinicians and institutions. The finetuned diffusion model also competes with leading vision-language models, highlighting its potential for improving medical report generation efficiency and flexibility.

entry.title: Researchers demonstrate Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards improving tool-use agent performance on synthetic Atlassian Jira and Confluence API workflows [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) can significantly improve the performance of tool-use agents in synthetic environments simulating Atlassian Jira and Confluence APIs. By applying RLVR directly within these target environments, the study addresses the limitations of large language models trained solely for next-token prediction, which often fail silently in complex enterprise SaaS workflows requiring precise API interactions. The RL-trained policies showed marked improvements in average rewards, particularly in scenarios like Confluence page creation, indicating more reliable and accurate API usage by the agents. The research involved creating five synthetic environments that replicate the Jira REST v3 and Confluence v2 APIs with high schema fidelity, using rewards computed solely from tool-call traces without live APIs, learned judges, or human labels. Testing on prompted Qwen3 models revealed that RLVR enhanced performance across most scenarios, though the approach currently faces scalability challenges due to the manual effort required to craft verifiable rewards and limitations in certain reward structures. This work represents an initial step toward developing outcome-optimized small models tailored for niche enterprise APIs.

entry.title: Researchers diagnose reinforcement learning limitations in clinical protocol tasks using MedAgentBench-v3 with 508 FHIR-based tasks and identify capability and format-knowledge barriers [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have evaluated reinforcement learning (RL) methods on clinical protocol-execution tasks using MedAgentBench, a benchmark based on FHIR standards. They identified significant limitations in earlier versions, including a high rate of silent finishes that favored inaction. To address this, they developed MedAgentBench-v3 with 508 tasks and a lower silent-finish rate, revealing two main barriers to RL performance: a capability ceiling where many task types showed no learning progress, and a format-knowledge barrier requiring exact clinical codes that RL could not discover through exploration. Experiments with the Qwen3-8B model showed that pure RL achieved a 18.2% success rate compared to 34.1% for rule-based supervised fine-tuning (SFT), with the performance gap attributed entirely to these structural barriers. The study proposes a taxonomy combining decision-making, format knowledge, and lookup requirements to predict RL learnability and suggests combining SFT to provide necessary clinical codes with RL to learn conditional logic as a solution to improve clinical agent performance.

entry.title: Researchers propose Procedural Memory Distillation to improve language model training by converting cross-episode signals into reusable memory, boosting performance on Qwen3-8B and OLMo3-Instruct-7B benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Procedural Memory Distillation (PMD), a novel training method for language models that captures and reuses procedural information across multiple episodes to enhance learning. Unlike traditional reinforcement learning approaches that update policies based only on individual episode signals, PMD distills cross-episode insights into reusable memory, which is then integrated into the model's parameters, resulting in improved performance without requiring memory at inference. PMD organizes procedural memory at three abstraction levels-raw trajectories, self-reflected strategies, and recurring behavioral patterns-extracted online from the model's own experiences. A memory-conditioned self-teacher uses this accumulated knowledge to guide the model's training, enabling a co-evolution process where the policy and memory iteratively improve each other. Experiments on Qwen3-8B and OLMo3-Instruct-7B models demonstrate that PMD outperforms previous methods by significant margins on benchmarks like SCIKNOWEVAL and LIVECODEBENCH, with co-evolution playing a critical role in these gains.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Agentic Bootstrap using AI agents to reveal analytical variation and assess scientific credibility across multiple analysis paths in empirical research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Agentic Bootstrap, a method using AI agents to explore the range of plausible analytical choices in empirical research and assess scientific credibility. By simulating different researcher personas, AI agents revealed how varying analysis paths can lead to divergent conclusions from the same data, mirroring ideological differences observed among human research teams. This approach highlights that the challenge in empirical studies often lies not in flawed analyses but in selective reporting from many defensible methods. The study applied Agentic Bootstrap to a dataset on immigration analyzed by 42 human teams, finding that AI agents reproduced 72% of the ideological variation in reported effects. Most AI-generated analyses passed independent AI and human expert reviews, underscoring the difficulty of identifying clear flaws in individual analyses. To quantify the extremity of reported findings, the researchers introduced the m-value, representing the probability that an analysis path would yield a claim as extreme as the one reported. Agentic Bootstrap makes the distribution of possible analyses visible, suggesting that scientific evidence should be evaluated in the context of this broader analytical landscape rather than a single reported result. This method offers a new criterion for assessing the robustness and credibility of empirical findings by accounting for the multiverse of reasonable analytical choices.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Janus, a modular system and evaluation framework for user-involved agentic permission management in AI, highlighting the importance of user input and context-sensitive designs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Janus, a modular system and evaluation framework designed to explore user-involved permission management in AI agents that act autonomously on behalf of users. Janus includes Janus-Core, which supports various permission management designs, and Janus-Harness, an automated tool for evaluating these designs. The system implements six permission assistants and tests them across multiple scenarios, emphasizing the critical role of user input in enhancing privacy and security. The study highlights that augmenting user decisions with AI can reduce cognitive load, but also notes the importance of accounting for realistic user behaviors such as permission fatigue. Findings indicate that no single permission management design is optimal in all contexts, underscoring the need for context-sensitive approaches when deploying such systems. Janus is publicly available to facilitate further research in this area of agentic system design.

entry.title: Researchers propose Semi-CoT, a semi-supervised chain-of-thought learning framework using unlabeled questions to generate pseudo reasoning supervision with high-precision pseudo-answers in pilot experiments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Semi-CoT, a semi-supervised chain-of-thought learning framework that leverages unlabeled questions to generate pseudo reasoning supervision with high-precision pseudo-answers. This approach extends traditional chain-of-thought methods by using reasoning chains not only as inference-time prompts but also as semi-supervised learning signals, selecting reliable pseudo reasoning chains based on low semantic entropy. Pilot experiments on datasets including AQuA, SVAMP, GSM8K, and MultiArith demonstrated that Semi-CoT effectively identifies high-precision pseudo reasoning chains, achieving pseudo-answer precision between 91.36% and 100%. While the method showed modest improvements on some datasets, results varied, indicating that further refinement in demonstration selection and training is needed to fully harness unlabeled questions for reasoning supervision.

entry.title: Researchers introduce OPINE-World, an LLM agent that learns object-centric programmatic world models online using ontology-error-prioritized exploration, solving 20 of 25 ARC-AGI-3 benchmark games without per-game training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed OPINE-World, a large language model (LLM) agent that learns object-centric programmatic world models through online interaction using a novel exploration strategy called ontology-error-prioritized exploration. This approach combines two cooperating agents-one interacting with the environment and the other synthesizing the world model in code-enabling efficient hypothesis testing and model refinement. OPINE-World was evaluated on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, which challenges agents to acquire skills without prior knowledge of object vocabulary, goals, or action semantics, and successfully solved 20 out of 25 games without per-game training, achieving an action-efficiency score close to human performance. Unlike traditional deep network-based world models that require large amounts of data and struggle to generalize, OPINE-World leverages program synthesis refined by counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) to create reusable and data-efficient models. Its exploration is guided by a Bayesian measure of object-type adequacy called ontology error, allowing it to hypothesize flexible object structures in pixel-rendered environments. This method demonstrates a significant advance in building adaptive agents capable of learning and planning in complex, unfamiliar settings.

entry.title: Researchers scale SOLiD lie detector oversight for preference learning in LLMs, reducing undetected deception from 34% to 14% between 1B and 405B parameter models, but note sensitivity to data distribution shifts [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have advanced the Scalable Oversight via Lie Detectors (SOLiD) method to monitor deceptive behavior in large language models (LLMs), demonstrating improved effectiveness as model size increases. Their study shows that undetected deception decreases from 34% in 1-billion-parameter models to 14% in 405-billion-parameter models, with a high true positive rate of 99%, allowing the removal of costly human labelers during fine-tuning without significantly increasing deception. However, the researchers note that SOLiD's performance is sensitive to shifts in data distribution between the detector's training data and the preference-learning data, which can lead to impractically high false positive rates. This highlights challenges in maintaining detector reliability across varying data conditions in preference learning for LLMs.

entry.title: Researchers present EO-Agents, a three-agent LLM pipeline using NASA Earth Observation Knowledge Graph to generate and evaluate 160 scientific hypotheses across multiple Earth science domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed EO-Agents, a three-agent large language model (LLM) pipeline that generates and evaluates scientific hypotheses grounded in the NASA Earth Observation Knowledge Graph. By leveraging a heterogeneous graph neural network trained on historical dataset co-usage, the system ranks candidate dataset pairings and produces 160 hypotheses across diverse Earth science domains such as ecohydrology, glaciology, and stratospheric chemistry. This approach enables the identification of scientifically coherent but previously unexplored dataset combinations. The pipeline was applied to 1,475 NASA datasets, and model-predicted novel pairings were found to be nearly as plausible as real co-usages documented in the literature. A factorial experiment comparing GPT-5.2 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 demonstrated stable hypothesis rankings, though absolute evaluation scores varied depending on the judge, highlighting challenges in single-judge LLM assessments.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Hawk, a training-free framework that improves NPU kernel generation accuracy from 49.4% to 80% and achieves up to 2.2x speedup by leveraging hardware-aware knowledge [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Hawk, a training-free framework designed to improve the generation of high-performance kernels for Neural Processing Units (NPUs). Hawk addresses the challenges posed by implicit hardware constraints and strict memory hierarchies that often cause large language models to fail on NPUs. By integrating hardware-aware knowledge through three specialized modules, Hawk significantly increases kernel generation accuracy from 49.4% to 80% and achieves up to a 2.2 times speedup compared to existing methods. The framework includes a Run-Time Knowledge Synthesis Module that links error context with executable semantics, a Bottleneck-Aware Knowledge Retrieval Module that projects queries into syntactic and hardware-aligned semantic spaces, and an Effect-Driven Knowledge Distillation Module that refines knowledge using execution feedback. Evaluations on real-world NPU workloads demonstrate Hawk's effectiveness in enhancing both accuracy and execution speed, offering a promising solution to the industry's kernel development bottleneck.

entry.title: Researchers propose PASE, a neuro-symbolic framework using LLMs and a neural-symbolic world model to verify and optimize cloud recovery plans, reducing system recovery time by over 40% in fault injection tests [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed PASE, a novel neuro-symbolic framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with a neural-symbolic world model to generate, verify, and optimize cloud system recovery plans. This approach treats recovery as a program synthesis task, using an LLM to create structured plans, a world model to simulate and verify these plans, and a reinforcement learning-based optimizer to refine the planning prompts. In tests involving real-world cloud fault injections, PASE reduced system recovery time by over 40% and improved fault detection accuracy compared to existing methods. PASE's tightly coupled reason-plan-verify-adapt loop enables dynamic and context-aware recovery strategies that go beyond predefined actions. By combining LLM-based reasoning with model-assisted verification and meta-learned guidance, the framework advances autonomous management of complex cloud-based AI systems, addressing the growing challenges of fault detection and adaptive recovery in large-scale environments.

entry.title: Researchers present SemHash-LLM, a multi-granularity semantic hashing framework combining LLM embeddings and MinHash for efficient large-scale document deduplication with under 1% neural verification cost [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced SemHash-LLM, a multi-granularity semantic hashing framework designed for efficient large-scale document deduplication while preserving semantic equivalence. The approach integrates semantic projection hashing, attention-weighted MinHash, contrastive boundary learning, and selective large language model (LLM) adjudication to combine character, token, and document-level signals through gated fusion. This method applies a cascaded filtering pipeline to reduce candidate duplicates effectively, achieving strong duplicate detection quality with less than 1% neural verification cost. SemHash-LLM learns compact binary codes within a distilled LLM embedding space and uses attention-weighted MinHash to suppress boilerplate content and highlight informative sections. Adaptive decision boundaries and uncertainty estimation enhance robustness against challenges such as template pollution, short text perturbations, containment, and viral fragments. Experimental results demonstrate the framework's efficiency and accuracy in handling massive corpora for document deduplication tasks.

entry.title: Researchers propose profit-based counterfactual explanation framework to optimize product attributes for manga sales improvement in Japan [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a new framework called profit-based counterfactual explanation (PBCE) to improve product attributes and optimize manga sales in Japan. This approach addresses limitations in existing counterfactual explanation methods by framing the problem as profit maximization, eliminating the need for predefined target outputs and providing an economically meaningful interpretation of the costs involved in modifying product features. PBCE directly maximizes profit as the primary objective, reinterpreting the distance metric commonly used in counterfactual explanations as the cost of changing product attributes. This method enhances decision-making in management and marketing by focusing on optimizing outcomes rather than merely altering model predictions.

entry.title: Researchers propose C3RL algorithm to improve large language model confidence calibration and introduce CAS for adaptive test-time scaling, reducing inference costs by up to 12.33 times across eight datasets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a new reinforcement learning algorithm called C3RL (Correctness and Confidence Calibration Reinforcement Learning) to improve the confidence calibration of large language models (LLMs) without compromising their accuracy. This approach addresses the common issue where models become overconfident and hallucinate when uncertain, by integrating correctness, calibration, and dataset-informed accuracy rewards. Evaluations across eight text and multimodal datasets show that C3RL outperforms existing methods in both performance and calibration metrics. Building on C3RL, the team introduced Confidence-based Adaptive Test Time Scaling (CAS), an inference-time strategy that dynamically allocates computational resources based on the model's confidence. CAS demonstrated superior results compared to majority voting on both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets while reducing inference costs by up to 12.33 times. Together, C3RL and CAS offer a promising path toward more reliable and resource-efficient deployment of LLMs. The researchers plan to release the associated code, data, and models.

entry.title: Researchers propose geometry-aware graph neural network for fine-scale rainfall reconstruction, reducing RMSE by 23.2% on Singapore data and generalizing to Sydney conditions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a geometry-aware multi-support heterogeneous graph neural network to improve fine-scale rainfall reconstruction, which is essential for urban flood modeling. This approach accounts for the different spatial supports of rainfall measurements-points from gauges, lines from microwave links, and grids from radar or satellite data-by representing each as distinct node layers and fusing them through cross-support message passing. Tested on Singapore data, the method reduced the root mean square error (RMSE) by 23.2% compared to traditional interpolation methods and outperformed other neural network architectures. The model's design allows it to reconstruct rainfall fields at user-defined locations, independent of the sensing resolution. A generalization study using data from Sydney, Australia, revealed that the benefits of multi-support fusion depend on the spacing of gauges relative to the spatial correlation length of rainfall, with the greatest improvements occurring when the field is under-sampled. The researchers plan to open-source their code and models upon paper acceptance.

entry.title: Researchers present TrafficSci, an AI system that autonomously rediscovers traffic laws and identifies new urban driving behavior patterns across eight cities and multiple datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed TrafficSci, an autonomous AI system designed to discover traffic laws by analyzing urban driving patterns across multiple cities and datasets. TrafficSci operates through an iterative process that includes evidence gathering, hypothesis testing, and validation, enabling it to independently rediscover known traffic laws and uncover a previously unreported temporal memory scale in driving behavior. The system was tested in four case studies covering various scales such as population, network, control, and trajectory, demonstrating consistent findings across eight cities and two trajectory datasets. TrafficSci represents a significant advancement in applying AI-driven scientific discovery to complex urban transportation systems, moving beyond controlled laboratory environments to real-world applications.

entry.title: Researchers propose InfoDelphi framework using information asymmetry in multi-agent systems to improve forecasting accuracy by up to 18% on real-world prediction benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced InfoDelphi, a new framework that enhances forecasting accuracy in multi-agent systems by leveraging information asymmetry. Unlike traditional methods where all agents receive identical evidence, InfoDelphi partitions information into shared public and private subsets, ensuring each agent holds unique knowledge that must be shared through deliberation. This approach reduces error correlation among agents and improves collective reasoning. InfoDelphi combines relevance-aware evidence routing, iterative deliberation based on rationales, and confidence-weighted aggregation. Tested on PolyGym, a benchmark with 375 binary forecasting questions from real-world prediction markets, it outperformed leading single-agent and multi-agent models by 12 to 18% in Brier score and increased accuracy by 4 to 8 percentage points. Further experiments confirmed that removing information asymmetry significantly diminishes the benefits of multi-agent deliberation, highlighting the importance of diverse input for effective forecasting.

entry.title: Researchers propose incremental expert bank method for continual ECG deployment without raw ECG replay, separating expert retention from autonomous source inference challenges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed an incremental expert bank method for continual deployment of ECG models that avoids replaying raw ECG data. Their approach freezes a pretrained backbone and assigns isolated classifiers to each data source, addressing parameter interference while enabling expert selection without source metadata. The method uses frozen ECG features and adds a balanced-softmax linear expert for each new domain, with a lightweight router trained on retained features and domain labels to select experts, improving performance on multiple ECG datasets.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Goggles, a pretrained module that edits finetuning gradients to impart epistemic frames on language models, improving fictional content recognition from 9% to 91% accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Goggles, a pretrained module that modifies finetuning gradients to instill an epistemic frame in language models, significantly improving their ability to recognize fictional content. Traditional finetuning on documents labeled as fictional results in models that still accept the core claims as true only about 9% of the time. Goggles intervenes during finetuning by editing the gradients, enabling the model to correctly identify fictional content approximately 91% of the time while maintaining overall performance on other benchmarks. Goggles is trained once for a specific base model and configuration, then applied to new documents without requiring fictional annotations. Beyond fiction detection, the module can impart other epistemic frames, such as treating documents as part of an AI safety evaluation. This approach offers a promising method for training language models on misaligned data without adopting undesirable behaviors, as the imparted frame remains stable even under further finetuning that might otherwise reverse such interventions.

entry.title: Researchers introduce COMFYCLAW, a self-evolving skill harness for ComfyUI image generation workflows that improves agent reliability and outperforms verifier-only baselines across multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed COMFYCLAW, a self-evolving skill harness designed to enhance the reliability and performance of agents controlling ComfyUI image generation workflows. COMFYCLAW improves workflow construction by using typed graph editing, organized tools, automatic correction of invalid edits, and a vision-language model verifier that translates visual errors into repair suggestions. It also evolves a skill library by learning from previous runs, which helps agents recall workflow patterns and user preferences. The framework was tested across multiple benchmarks, agent models, and image backbones, consistently outperforming verifier-only baselines. Human evaluations further favored COMFYCLAW over versions without skill evolution, indicating that evolving reusable skills significantly boosts agent effectiveness in recurring visual workflow tasks. These findings suggest that skill evolution is a promising approach to improving agent-assisted workflows, particularly in domain-specific, repetitive tasks such as image generation, by enabling agents to adapt and refine their capabilities over time.

entry.title: Researchers propose Generic TB-Coverage method for pruning sparse Mixture-of-Experts language models using generic text corpora, improving zero-shot accuracy and reducing perplexity without downstream calibration data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Generic TB-Coverage, a new method for pruning sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models using only generic text corpora like WikiText2 and C4 for calibration. This approach avoids relying on a single aggregated importance score by profiling each expert's utility separately across different corpora and enforcing a coverage rule to retain high-utility experts from each dataset. The method improves zero-shot accuracy and reduces perplexity degradation compared to existing pruning techniques, especially under aggressive pruning conditions. The study tested Generic TB-Coverage on Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B and DeepSeek-MoE-16B-Base models at various retention levels (25%, 50%, and 75%), demonstrating consistent gains over random pruning, REAP, and ExpertSparsity methods. These results suggest that maintaining cross-corpus expert coverage serves as an effective generic-data prior for MoE pruning, enabling improvements without the need for downstream calibration data.

entry.title: Researchers propose a distributionally robust listwise preference optimization method for language model alignment that improves ranking robustness under label uncertainty and noise [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a distributionally robust listwise preference optimization method to improve language model alignment under ranking-label uncertainty. This approach addresses ambiguities in observed rankings caused by annotator inconsistency, near-ties, lossy feedback, or noise in reward models by introducing a robust Plackett--Luce objective that enhances ranking robustness directly on the candidate list. The method simplifies the computational complexity of worst-case ranking evaluation and provides strong theoretical guarantees for both offline and online optimization settings. Experiments demonstrate that this robust optimization preserves performance with clean labels and significantly improves resilience to noisy data in offline language model alignment. In online scenarios, it enhances the reliability of reward-model-ranked candidate expansions and boosts evaluation metrics from both the reward model and external GPT-4 judges, indicating its practical effectiveness in refining language model training under uncertain preference signals.

entry.title: Researchers propose DRL-CLBA, a clean label backdoor attack using DDPG reinforcement learning and audio steganography to bypass defenses in speech classification models [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed DRL-CLBA, a new clean label backdoor attack targeting speech classification models. This method uses Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) reinforcement learning combined with deep audio steganography to embed sample-specific triggers into audio data, enabling the attack to bypass many existing defenses without altering labels. The approach optimizes target samples in the model's latent space to create effective backdoor triggers that cause misclassification during inference. Tests on three datasets and four different deep neural networks show that DRL-CLBA achieves a high success rate and resists common countermeasures such as fine-tuning, pruning, and spectral signature detection. This exposes significant vulnerabilities in speech-controlled systems and highlights the need for improved security measures against sophisticated backdoor attacks in audio-based AI applications.

entry.title: arXiv:2607.01734 presents reformalizations of the Jordan Curve Theorem from Mizar and HOL Light to Lean and Agda, analyzing pipeline design choices for proof assistant translation
entry.summary: The paper on arXiv titled "Reformalization of the Jordan Curve Theorem" presents a case study in reformalization, where formal proofs from one proof assistant are translated into another. Specifically, it details three reformalizations of the Jordan Curve Theorem: from Mizar to Lean, from HOL Light to Lean, and from HOL Light to Agda. The study analyzes these efforts and highlights key pipeline design choices that influence the effectiveness of practical reformalization tasks. This work explores a variant of autoformalization that uses formal developments rather than natural language as input, providing insights into the challenges and strategies involved in translating proofs across different formal systems. The findings contribute to understanding how to improve interoperability and automation in formal proof verification.

entry.title: Researchers present a meta-benchmarking framework organizing 452 financial-services LLM benchmarks into 38 banking domains, evaluating 288 models across 25 organizations as of June 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a meta-benchmarking framework that organizes 452 publicly reported benchmarks into 38 banking business domains, covering areas such as sales, operations, risk, and support. This framework evaluates 288 large language models (LLMs) from 25 organizations as of June 2026, addressing the specific cognitive demands of financial services that are often overlooked by general LLM leaderboards. The approach uses a weighting scheme to prioritize benchmarks that remain relevant and discriminative, enabling cross-benchmark comparisons without raw score normalization. The framework aggregates benchmarks into 41 generalized work activities based on O*NET classifications and applies a pairwise Elo tournament system to generate comparable scores across different tasks. This method suppresses outdated tests and produces weighted averages for business domain scores. The researchers provide detailed methodology, taxonomy, and design considerations to support reproducibility and assist institutions in model selection and governance within the financial sector.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Phi-Nav, a hindsight reasoning framework for Vision-Language Navigation that aligns instructions with exploratory trajectories, improving training efficiency on R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Phi-Nav, a novel framework for Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) that improves training efficiency by aligning language instructions with the agent's actual exploratory paths. Phi-Nav uses a three-stage process involving oracle-guided exploration, synthesis of hindsight instructions based on observed trajectories, and a second imitation learning phase with these synthesized instructions. This approach addresses the semantic mismatch between executed trajectories and original instructions common in on-policy exploration. Evaluations on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks demonstrate that Phi-Nav achieves competitive performance while requiring significantly fewer expert demonstrations than existing methods. By converting unlabeled exploratory movements into meaningful training signals, Phi-Nav enhances semantic exploration in VLN and offers an effective solution for training embodied agents with limited data.

entry.title: Researchers present Mastermind, a strategy-grounded learning framework that improves repository-scale vulnerability reproduction with up to 84.5% pass rate using GPT-5.5 executor [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Mastermind, a novel learning framework designed to enhance repository-scale vulnerability reproduction in software engineering. Mastermind focuses on learning high-level strategies rather than full action sequences, enabling an agent to inspect codebases, infer input grammars, construct proof-of-concept exploits, and verify fixes more effectively. Using a dual-loop approach, the framework separates transferable strategy learning from task-specific experience, allowing a trainable planner to improve multiple executors without altering their action capabilities. Evaluated on the CyberGym benchmark with 260 training and 200 evaluation tasks, Mastermind achieved an 84.5% success rate using GPT-5.5 as the executor, significantly outperforming existing methods such as open-book proof-of-concept context and iterative improvement. The framework also improved performance for other models like GPT-5.4 mini and GLM 5.1, demonstrating that learning reusable strategies is an effective and transferable method for advancing software vulnerability reproduction agents.

entry.title: Researchers present SimWorlds, a multi-agent system generating dynamic, editable 4D scenes from text with Blender integration and introduce 4DBuildBench benchmark for visual and physical fidelity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed SimWorlds, a multi-agent system that generates dynamic, editable 4D scenes from text inputs, integrating procedural knowledge specific to Blender. This system addresses the challenges of coordinating spatial layout, physics solvers, temporal sequencing, camera, and lighting to create coherent scenes featuring moving liquids, particles, and mechanisms. SimWorlds employs a planner-coder-reviewer workflow, a layered scene protocol with deterministic verification, and runtime inspection tools to detect issues not visible in rendered images. Alongside SimWorlds, the team introduced 4DBuildBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate both the visual fidelity and physical consistency of procedurally generated dynamic 3D scenes from text prompts. Experimental results demonstrate that SimWorlds outperforms previous dynamic Blender generation methods, advancing the creation of physics-grounded, editable content useful for video generation and embodied AI applications.

entry.title: Researchers propose WM-SAR method to repair agent planning graphs by targeting error-amplifying subgraphs, outperforming traditional LLM repair approaches under realistic token budgets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced WM-SAR (World-Model Subgraph Amplification Repair), a novel method for correcting errors in large agent planning graphs by targeting the subgraphs that amplify errors rather than addressing visible symptoms. This approach outperforms traditional engineering methods that scan and repair suspicious local regions, especially under realistic token budget constraints, by focusing on the causal subgraph responsible for persistent errors and enabling more efficient and stable repairs. The study compares WM-SAR with conventional LLM-based correctors, demonstrating that while engineering correctors can be effective with large context sizes, WM-SAR achieves near-complete graph stabilization with a smaller, more focused repair region. This method reduces computational overhead and improves the quality of repairs by providing the language model with a cleaner and more relevant repair target, addressing challenges in persistent workflows involving thousands of planning steps.

entry.title: Researchers propose retrieval-augmented small language model framework using formal concept analysis for verifiable knowledge expansion with evaluation on rare ataxia data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a retrieval-augmented small language model (SLM) framework that integrates formal concept analysis (FCA) to verify and expand knowledge structures derived from text. This approach uses FCA to propose logical implications based on seed attributes, which are then validated or refuted by a retrieval-grounded SLM oracle, allowing for inspection of accepted implications, counterexamples, and corrections. The framework was evaluated using rare ataxia data from Orphadata, achieving relation F1 scores between 0.29 and 0.52 and implication F1 scores between 0.22 and 0.30, with larger seed sets improving performance.

entry.title: Researchers find Diffusion Language Models internally encode latent timestep representations related to denoising progress, enabling modulation of model confidence and entropy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have discovered that Diffusion Language Models (DLMs), which are emerging as an alternative to autoregressive models, internally encode a latent representation related to the diffusion timestep despite not being explicitly conditioned on it. This latent signal, found within the models' residual streams, can be reliably extracted and decoded, indicating that DLMs track denoising progress internally. By manipulating this representation, the researchers were able to systematically influence the model's confidence and entropy during generation. The study further analyzed the geometric structure of this latent timestep representation in activation space, revealing interpretable and organized properties that shed light on how DLMs process denoising information. These findings enhance understanding of the internal mechanisms of diffusion-based language models and suggest new ways to control their behavior through latent time modulation.

entry.title: Researchers present Vera, an automated safety testing framework for LLM agents, revealing 93.9% average attack success rates across four production frameworks and releasing Vera-Bench with 1600 safety cases [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Vera, an automated safety testing framework designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents that perform autonomous actions through external tools. Vera uses a three-stage pipeline to discover emerging safety risks, generate executable safety cases, and adaptively test agents in isolated environments. Testing across four production agent frameworks revealed significant safety vulnerabilities, with attack success rates averaging 93.9%. Alongside Vera, the team released Vera-Bench, a comprehensive suite of 1600 safety cases covering 124 risk categories to support ongoing evaluation. Vera's approach integrates software engineering testing principles tailored for non-deterministic agents, employing evidence-based verification rather than relying on model self-reports. This modular and scalable infrastructure addresses the challenges of evolving agent behaviors and complex safety risks. The framework and benchmark are publicly available, providing a valuable resource for rigorous safety assessment of rapidly advancing agentic systems.

entry.title: Researchers introduce MMIR-TCM, a multimodal AI framework integrating memory-augmented segmentation and retrieval-augmented generation for Traditional Chinese Medicine diagnosis, validated on a new large-scale MedTCM dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed MMIR-TCM, a multimodal AI framework designed to improve Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnosis by integrating memory-augmented segmentation and retrieval-augmented generation. This system mimics expert diagnostic processes by combining a training-free tongue segmentation module, a fine-tuned model for structured diagnosis, and an evidence-based clinical decision support component. The framework was validated using MedTCM, a newly introduced large-scale multimodal dataset for TCM research, and evaluated with a novel domain-specific metric, TDEU, to better capture clinical accuracy. MMIR-TCM addresses challenges in TCM diagnosis, such as subjectivity and the semantic gap between visual tongue features and textual reasoning, which have hindered the application of AI in this field. Experimental results show that MMIR-TCM outperforms leading models like GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash, demonstrating its potential to enhance syndrome differentiation and prescription generation in TCM clinical practice.

entry.title: Researchers release Pre-Flight, an open source benchmark of 300 questions evaluating large language models on aviation operational knowledge, showing top models reach 82.7% accuracy versus 95% expert level [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Pre-Flight, an open source benchmark consisting of 300 multiple-choice questions designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on aviation operational knowledge. The benchmark covers topics such as international airport ground operations, ICAO and US FAA regulations, and complex operational scenarios, with questions developed and reviewed by aviation professionals. Testing various commercial and open models revealed that the best-performing model achieved 82.7% accuracy, compared to an expert reference accuracy of about 95%, indicating a notable gap in model reliability for this specialized domain. Pre-Flight aims to address the limitations of general-purpose benchmarks by focusing on the high-stakes, regulated aviation sector where safe and accurate reasoning is critical. The dataset, evaluation tools, and results are publicly available through the Inspect evaluation framework, with ongoing updates as new models emerge. The researchers emphasize that domain-specific evaluation is essential for the responsible deployment of generative AI in non-safety-critical aviation operations, highlighting the need for continued improvement in model performance within this field.

entry.title: Researchers apply Halpern & Pearl's actual causality theory to fault trees, classifying causality notions and linking minimal cut sets to actual causes for failure diagnostics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have applied Halpern and Pearl's theory of actual causality to fault trees, which are commonly used risk models for complex systems. This approach enables fault trees to address not only what can go wrong but also why failures occur, enhancing failure diagnostics. The study provides a comprehensive classification of different notions of actual causality based on the fault tree's graph and logical structures, demonstrating how minimal cut sets correspond to actual causes of system failures. By linking minimal cut sets to actual causes, the research offers a deeper understanding of failure mechanisms within complex systems. This connection allows for more precise identification of causal factors in fault trees, potentially improving risk assessment and diagnostic processes in engineering and safety-critical applications.

entry.title: Researchers present CLAP, a closed-loop method for domain agent post-training that integrates data validation, evaluation, and release control to manage adapter suitability and risks in manufacturing scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced CLAP (Closed-Loop Agent Post-training), a method designed to improve domain agent performance by integrating data validation, evaluation, and release control into a continuous loop. This approach addresses challenges such as noisy business data, uncertain post-training benefits, and risks associated with deploying adapters in manufacturing scenarios. CLAP transforms business data into structured samples and diagnostics to determine adapter suitability for specific application chains. Testing CLAP on five anonymized manufacturing batches showed modest improvements in overall scores, pass rates, and evidence accuracy, while reducing hallucinations and factual errors. However, only some batches improved, highlighting risks like high KL divergence detected by GRPO. Further analysis demonstrated that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is essential for accurate factual extraction, with RAG-oriented adapters enhancing key metrics despite increased latency. These findings suggest that managing domain-agent post-training through an integrated data-training-evaluation-release cycle is more effective than relying solely on training completion or single offline metrics, offering a more reliable framework for deploying domain-specific AI adapters in complex environments.

entry.title: Researchers introduce STEER, a gradient-guided attack exploiting English-centric safety training in large language models, achieving up to 96.7% success on multilingual jailbreak benchmarks and transferring to GPT-4o-mini [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed STEER, a gradient-guided attack that exploits the English-centric safety training of large language models (LLMs) by translating key refusal-triggering words into low-resource languages. This method significantly reduces the models' refusal to generate harmful content, achieving success rates up to 96.7% on multilingual jailbreak benchmarks and demonstrating transferability to GPT-4o-mini with a 35.5% success rate without direct access to the model. The study highlights a critical gap in LLM safety mechanisms, which are primarily trained in English and may not generalize well to multilingual or code-switched inputs. STEER works by identifying words that strongly influence a model's refusal behavior and iteratively replacing them with translations in low-resource languages, preserving the harmful intent while bypassing safety filters. Tested across six open-source 8B-parameter models, STEER outperforms other attack methods like random code-switching and Greedy Coordinate Gradient. The findings suggest that the vulnerability is not limited to a single model architecture but is a broader issue stemming from the limited linguistic scope of current safety training. The researchers argue that enhancing multilingual safety in LLMs requires broader alignment coverage across diverse languages and the development of mechanisms that can detect and abstain from responding to out-of-distribution inputs. This work underscores the need for more inclusive safety training to prevent harmful outputs in multilingual contexts.

entry.title: Researchers introduce CamoNAS, a frequency-aware neural architecture search framework for camouflaged object detection achieving state-of-the-art results on four benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed CamoNAS, a frequency-aware neural architecture search (NAS) framework designed to improve camouflaged object detection (COD). CamoNAS automatically optimizes both cell-level operations and network-level downsampling paths within a hierarchical search space, enhancing the detection of objects that blend into their surroundings. The framework incorporates an RGB frequency dual-stream architecture, combining a learnable wavelet transform with the RGB spatial stream to better capture subtle features. CamoNAS demonstrated state-of-the-art performance across four COD benchmarks-CAMO, COD10K, NC4K, and CHAMELEON-surpassing traditional models that rely on hand-designed architectures and multi-scale feature fusion. This work highlights the potential of NAS techniques to systematically improve COD tasks, and the researchers have made their code publicly available for further exploration and development.

entry.title: Researchers introduce SkillCoach, a self-evolving rubric framework to evaluate and enhance agentic skill-use in LLM agents by analyzing skill selection, following, composition, and reflection [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed SkillCoach, a self-evolving rubric framework designed to evaluate and improve the use of skills by large language model (LLM) agents. SkillCoach assesses agentic skill-use across four key dimensions: skill selection, skill following, skill composition, and skill-grounded reflection, distinguishing process quality from mere task success. This approach addresses challenges posed by overlapping skills in realistic repositories, where traditional final verifier success metrics are too coarse for effective evaluation and training. SkillCoach generates skill-grounded process rubrics from actual agent rollouts and uses these rubrics to supervise the selection of high-quality training trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that these evolved rubrics enhance evaluation accuracy, reveal failures that final accuracy metrics miss, and provide stronger supervision signals than outcome-only filtering methods, thereby advancing the reliability and effectiveness of skill use in LLM agents.

entry.title: Researchers propose Spec-AUF training method to improve masked block drafters by focusing cross-entropy loss on accepted token prefixes, boosting performance on Qwen3-8B benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Spec-AUF, a training method designed to improve masked block drafters used in speculative decoding for autoregressive generation. This approach focuses the cross-entropy loss on the accepted token prefixes rather than the entire predicted block, aligning training more closely with inference behavior where only the longest accepted prefix is committed. Applied to the Qwen3-8B model, Spec-AUF enhanced the average emitted token length across multiple benchmarks, demonstrating consistent performance gains without altering the inference pipeline or requiring auxiliary objectives. Spec-AUF addresses the mismatch between training and inference by truncating the cross-entropy support at the first predicted failure, approximating prefix-sensitive supervision in mask-only block drafters that lack input-side conditioning. Experiments showed that this targeted supervision improves decoding efficiency and accuracy compared to traditional full-block loss training and recent acceptance-aware objectives. The method also revealed that standard position-decay weighting becomes less effective once the loss support is truncated, highlighting new insights into training dynamics for block drafters.

entry.title: Researchers present HECATE, a tool measuring complexity in LLM-integrated applications by assessing both prompt and code layers, validating new metrics that predict maintenance effort beyond code size [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed HECATE, a novel tool designed to measure complexity in applications that integrate large language models (LLMs) by evaluating both the natural language prompt layer and the program code. Unlike traditional complexity metrics that focus solely on code, HECATE uses a formalism called Prompt-as-Specification to treat prompts as behavioral specifications, generating metrics that capture structural elements such as LLM call sites and prompt templates. This approach identifies complexity dimensions overlooked by existing methods and better predicts maintenance effort. The team tested 52 candidate metrics across 118 components from 18 open-source repositories, using maintenance activity as a proxy for complexity. After controlling for code size, only ten metrics remained significant, with seven newly introduced metrics emphasizing structural breadth rather than volume. These prompt-layer metrics maintained their predictive power even when combined with the strongest code-level metrics, confirming that prompt complexity is an independent factor. Validation on additional repositories demonstrated the generalizability of the top metrics in forecasting maintenance demands.

entry.title: AntTrail introduces ContextSniper, a token-efficient code memory layer for repository-level program repair that reduces token use by up to 51.5% with minor impact on resolution rates [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: AntTrail has introduced ContextSniper, a token-efficient code memory layer designed to improve repository-level program repair by reducing token usage by up to 51.5% with only a minor decrease in resolution rates. ContextSniper enhances AntTrail's broader agent memory engine by precisely selecting relevant code and runtime evidence, filtering outputs through an intention-aware context gate, and delivering compact evidence packets while maintaining essential source context. The system was evaluated using SWE-bench Lite with OpenClaw and Claude Code agents, showing significant reductions in token use and associated costs-51.5% and 36.4% for OpenClaw, and 38.9% and 27.3% for Claude Code-while resolution rates slightly declined from 26.0% to 24.0% and 32.0% to 30.0%, respectively. ContextSniper's pilot testing scripts have been made publicly available to support further research and development.

entry.title: Researchers present ElephantAgent protocol to enforce contextual state continuity and defend against poisoning attacks in agentic AI systems using trusted hardware and auditability [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced ElephantAgent, a protocol designed to ensure contextual state continuity in agentic AI systems, addressing vulnerabilities from tool and memory poisoning attacks. By verifying the integrity of an agent's critical contextual state before processing queries, ElephantAgent aims to prevent malicious manipulation that could bias agent behavior. The protocol leverages replicated trusted hardware to maintain a secure ledger of authorized state transitions and detect unauthorized tampering. ElephantAgent extends previous state-continuity mechanisms by focusing on the evolving contextual state, including tool states and memory, which are essential for planning and execution in agentic systems. It also offers historical traceability, allowing for post-hoc audits and recovery to known-good states to mitigate in-band semantic abuses. This approach enhances the security and reliability of AI agents that depend on external tools and persistent memory.

entry.title: Researchers propose ATMA, a state-aware overlay to reduce ghost memory failures in long-term LLM agent memory, improving conflict accuracy and temporal F1 on new benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced ATMA, a state-aware overlay designed to address ghost memory failures in long-term memory systems for large language model (LLM) agents. Ghost memory occurs when outdated, current, and transitional facts coexist and confuse the memory retrieval process, leading to inaccurate responses. ATMA improves memory accuracy by maintaining distinct records of superseded and transitional information, constructing evidence packets aligned with the query's state, and labeling facts as current, historical, or transitional during question answering. The team developed a new benchmark called LTP (LoCoMo Temporal Plus) to measure ghost memory conflicts and evaluated ATMA's performance on this and the existing LoCoMo benchmark. Results showed significant improvements in conflict accuracy and temporal F1 scores when ATMA was integrated with the Graphiti memory system, indicating that explicitly managing state information can reduce memory errors that are otherwise hidden by overall question-answering accuracy. This approach highlights the importance of decoupling evaluation at the memory bank, retrieval, and answer levels to better understand and mitigate memory failures in persistent LLM agents.

entry.title: Researchers propose Atomic Task Graph, a unified framework for LLM-based agent planning and execution that improves task decomposition, parallel execution, and error localization using 7B-8B models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
