entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Atomic Task Graph (ATG), a unified framework designed to enhance planning and execution in large language model (LLM)-based agents. ATG explicitly represents task dependencies through directed acyclic graphs, enabling recursive task decomposition, parallel execution of independent subtasks, and efficient error localization and repair. This approach improves task decomposition, execution efficiency, and error handling without relying on larger models or task-specific fine-tuning. ATG maintains an evolving graph structure that traces the breakdown of high-level tasks into subtasks, allowing verified intermediate results to be reused and independent branches to run concurrently. When failures occur, the framework identifies and fixes only the affected parts, preserving validated results. Experiments demonstrate that ATG outperforms strong baselines in success rate and execution efficiency across multiple interactive benchmarks using only 7B-8B parameter models.

entry.title: Researchers release OntoLearner, a modular Python library for ontology learning with large language models, providing 180 ontologies across 22 domains and standardized benchmarking datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced OntoLearner, a modular Python library designed to advance ontology learning (OL) by integrating large language models (LLMs) with a unified framework for ontology access and standardized benchmarking. OntoLearner provides 180 machine-readable ontologies across 22 domains and includes datasets with train/dev/test splits for key OL tasks such as term typing, taxonomy discovery, and relation extraction. This infrastructure supports systematic evaluation and cross-domain research, addressing longstanding fragmentation in OL methods and evaluation. Using OntoLearner, the team conducted a large-scale empirical study involving 22 retrieval models and 12 LLMs, revealing that the main challenges in OL arise from the complexity of ontologies rather than model size or architecture. The study highlights a structural mismatch between how models encode knowledge and how ontologies organize it, suggesting that improving OL effectiveness depends on bridging this gap. OntoLearner is open-source under the MIT license and available on GitHub, offering a foundation for future research and development in ontology learning.

entry.title: Researchers propose ScopeEdit, a scope-aware online editor for multimodal large language models that controls semantic boundaries of edits to improve cross-modal transfer and stability with constant overhead [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced ScopeEdit, a novel scope-aware online editor designed for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to improve the control of semantic boundaries during knowledge editing. This approach addresses the challenge of injecting continuous visual-textual corrections with minimal disruption to unrelated model behaviors, enhancing cross-modal transfer and stability while maintaining constant computational overhead. ScopeEdit operates by decomposing each update into two branches: a modality-local absorption branch that ensures stable edit integration, and an evidence-gated shared generalization branch that enables cross-modal propagation only when visual and textual evidence align. This design leverages orthogonal low-rank spaces and efficient preconditioners to maintain performance. Extensive testing across various benchmarks and real-world scenarios demonstrates that ScopeEdit effectively balances in-scope cross-modal transfer with out-of-scope locality, preserving edit reliability and efficiency in complex vision-language architectures.

entry.title: Researchers propose deterministic episodic-to-semantic memory consolidation method that preserves cryptographically certified agent identity and reduces unproductive planning by nearly 80% in synthetic experiments [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a deterministic method for consolidating episodic memory into semantic knowledge in adaptive intelligent agents, ensuring that the agent's cryptographically certified identity remains unchanged. This approach treats memory consolidation as a function that updates a separate semantic knowledge layer without altering the agent's identity manifest, addressing challenges in regulated autonomous systems where identity integrity is critical. Synthetic experiments demonstrated that this method reduces unproductive planning attempts by nearly 80%, while maintaining auditability and confidence in the knowledge updates. The team provided a formal framework for the agent's representation, proved identity invariance, and designed a deterministic aggregation algorithm that produces auditable database entries with explicit confidence levels and provenance. Their validation showed consistent identity hashes across consolidation passes and significant efficiency gains compared to baseline methods. This knowledge-update discipline allows lessons to accumulate as queryable facts, supporting long-term operation of autonomic agents without identity drift, exemplified through a service agent case study.

entry.title: Researchers present a retrieval-augmented multi-agent assistant for traceable fault diagnosis in large-scale battery energy storage systems, improving reliability through task routing and hybrid data retrieval [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a traceable fault diagnosis assistant for large-scale battery energy storage systems (BESSs) that enhances reliability by integrating operational data, domain knowledge, visual evidence, and report generation. This system employs retrieval-augmented multi-agent reasoning with BESS-specific task routing, schema-constrained natural-language database access, and hybrid text-image retrieval to improve diagnostic accuracy and decision-making. The assistant addresses challenges in monitoring platforms that can detect threshold violations but often cannot determine the specific causes or necessary interventions for issues such as voltage inconsistency, resistance drift, short-circuit risk, capacity divergence, or thermal abnormalities. Preliminary internal evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the system's routing, database access, and diagnostic reasoning capabilities.

entry.title: Researchers propose InduceKV, a fixed-memory retrieval method for continual adaptation of multimodal large language models, improving performance under strict memory budgets across multiple tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced InduceKV, a novel fixed-memory retrieval method designed to enable continual adaptation of multimodal large language models (LLMs) without increasing the deployment footprint. InduceKV stores selected training data as compact, attention-ready memory entries that can be appended to the model's self-attention cache, allowing task-specific updates to be externalized while keeping the backbone model unchanged. This approach maintains a fixed memory budget and improves performance across various tasks including task-incremental instruction tuning, continual visual question answering, and domain-incremental adaptation. InduceKV employs a bilevel selection process to construct a compact inducing set that balances current-task relevance, retention of prior knowledge, and coverage within the retrieval space. The method consistently outperforms existing techniques such as parameter-efficient fine-tuning, mixture-of-experts, replay, and prompt-retrieval baselines under matched memory constraints. Additional evaluations confirm that the performance gains are not due to stronger backbone models or unbounded candidate pools, highlighting InduceKV's efficiency and scalability for continual learning in multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: Researchers identify hidden evidence-use forgetting in continual multimodal learning where accuracy persists but grounding shifts, proposing RCL framework to preserve evidence reliance without replay [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called "hidden evidence-use forgetting" in continual multimodal learning, where models maintain answer accuracy but shift away from the original evidence sources used for grounding. This issue highlights that standard metrics focusing only on answer correctness overlook changes in how models rely on visual, textual, OCR, chart, and document evidence. To address this, the team proposed RCL, a replay-free reliance-constrained continual learning framework that preserves both task performance and evidence reliance without increasing inference costs. RCL works by freezing the previous model checkpoint as a behavioral reference and estimating evidence-reliance profiles through counterfactual interventions. Evaluated across multiple benchmarks, including CoIN, COAST, and MCITlib, RCL consistently improved performance and reduced forgetting compared to other methods, while significantly lowering shifts in modality reliance and hidden forgetting rates. These findings suggest that effective continual multimodal learning requires maintaining the evidence pathways behind correct answers, not just the answers themselves.

entry.title: Researchers introduce PACE, a proxy benchmark framework that predicts agentic LLM performance using a small subset of non-agentic evaluation instances, reducing evaluation cost by over 99% [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed PACE, a proxy benchmark framework designed to predict the performance of agentic large language models (LLMs) using a small, carefully selected subset of non-agentic evaluation instances. This approach significantly reduces the cost and time required for evaluation, cutting expenses by over 99% compared to traditional agentic benchmarks like SWE-Bench and GAIA, which are costly and time-consuming to run. PACE constructs proxy benchmarks by selecting instances from existing non-agentic evaluations that best predict agentic benchmark performance through a regression model. The framework combines local and global instance-selection strategies to curate a compact subset of evaluation tasks. Experiments involving 14 models across multiple benchmarks demonstrated that PACE-Bench, the resulting proxy benchmark, achieves high prediction accuracy with a mean absolute error under 4%, strong correlation with actual agentic scores, and reliable model ranking, all at a fraction of the usual evaluation cost. This method enables practitioners to efficiently estimate agentic capabilities during model development and selection without the overhead of full agent evaluation. Additionally, analysis of the selected proxy instances provides insights into the unique skills required by different agentic benchmarks, potentially guiding future evaluation and model improvement efforts.

entry.title: Researchers propose Algebraic Decision Tree Counting for exhaustive global analysis of optimal decision trees with polynomial-time dynamic programming algorithm [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Algebraic Decision Tree Counting (ADTC), a formal framework for the exhaustive global analysis of optimal and near-optimal decision trees in Explainable AI. ADTC unifies tasks such as optimization, counting, and sampling into a sum-of-products computation over a semiring, enabling a comprehensive assessment of the hypothesis space despite its doubly exponential size relative to tree depth. Their dynamic programming algorithm achieves polynomial-time complexity in the number of features, making the approach computationally feasible. The framework incorporates model behavior tensors to manage complex constraints involving multiple tree metrics, capturing trade-offs among accuracy, size, and fairness. The researchers demonstrated the effectiveness of their software, emtrees, on real-world datasets, showing how ADTC supports evidence-based model selection in sensitive application areas by providing a detailed global landscape of decision tree models.

entry.title: Researchers propose Maven, a reinforcement learning framework with editable evidence memory that improves long-context reasoning by rewarding intermediate evidence-state transitions across Llama and Qwen models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Maven, a reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance long-context reasoning in language models by using an editable evidence memory. Unlike existing methods that reward only final answers or static evidence extraction, Maven provides rewards for intermediate evidence-state transitions, such as adding, linking, or dropping evidence, based on their contribution to improving answer support. This approach was tested on Llama and Qwen models across several benchmarks, where it outperformed traditional reinforcement learning and evidence-identification methods by generating more comprehensive evidence sets and reducing irrelevant information. Maven assigns rewards to specific action spans using a method called GRPO, crediting actions that add marginal gains, link evidence synergistically, or remove misleading information. The framework's focus on optimizing stateful evidence navigation rather than one-shot extraction demonstrates significant improvements in handling lengthy inputs, suggesting a promising direction for advancing long-context reasoning in AI models.

entry.title: Researchers propose SUNTA, a hierarchical video prediction model using surprise-based chunking that maintains accurate predictions over 250 timesteps in 2D and 3D tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced SUNTA, a hierarchical video prediction model that uses surprise-based chunking to improve long-horizon predictions. Unlike previous models that rely on fixed-length or similarity-based chunking, SUNTA determines chunk boundaries based on prediction errors, which better capture when longer-range context is needed. This approach addresses challenges such as hierarchical collapse during training and the lack of surprise signals during open-loop prediction by employing a decoupled training strategy and using internal inconsistency as a top-down surprise metric. Experiments on 2D and 3D video prediction tasks show that SUNTA significantly outperforms existing baselines, maintaining accurate predictions over 250 timesteps, whereas other models' performance deteriorates within the first 10 timesteps. This advancement suggests that surprise-based chunking can effectively enhance the temporal abstraction capabilities of hierarchical state-space models for complex video prediction tasks.

entry.title: Researchers present ContextNest, an open specification and implementation for verifiable context governance in autonomous AI agents, improving provenance and retrieval integrity [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced ContextNest, an open specification and reference implementation designed to enhance context governance in autonomous AI agents by ensuring verifiable provenance, version identity, integrity, and traceability of external knowledge sources. Unlike traditional retrieval methods that focus solely on relevance, ContextNest adds a governance layer beneath retrieval systems to verify that knowledge artifacts are approved, current, and integrity-verified before use. This approach combines typed Markdown documents, deterministic selectors, cryptographic version histories, and audit trails to enable organizations to reconstruct the exact knowledge versions that informed AI outputs. Empirical results from controlled experiments demonstrate that ContextNest's governed selection outperforms standard BM25 retrieval in answer quality while reducing input-token costs. Additionally, deterministic selectors provide stable document retrieval across repeated queries, addressing failure modes that retrieval quality alone cannot resolve. The researchers have released a core engine, command-line interface, and Model Context Protocol server under open licenses to support adoption and further development.

entry.title: Researchers introduce FitOne, domain-specific fitness LLMs with 8B and 32B parameters, improving performance on professional fitness certification exams by up to 12.73% through a three-stage post-training pipeline [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed FitOne, a series of domain-specific large language models (LLMs) with 8 billion and 32 billion parameters, aimed at enhancing scientific fitness coaching (SFC). Built on the Qwen3 foundation models, FitOne employs a three-stage post-training process-continual pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning-using extensive, high-quality datasets to improve performance on professional fitness certification exams by up to 12.73%. This approach addresses the limitations of general-purpose LLMs in handling complex fitness coaching scenarios by integrating specialized domain knowledge. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that FitOne maintains strong general capabilities while significantly outperforming base models on exams such as ACSM-EP and NSCA-CSCS. Ablation studies confirm the importance of each training stage in balancing domain expertise with general ability retention. This advancement represents a step toward more reliable and accessible fitness intelligence, potentially inspiring further development of domain-specific LLMs.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Paper-replication workflow enabling coding agents to replicate and validate computational claims in scientific machine learning papers across multiple runs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Paper-replication, a workflow designed to enable coding agents to replicate and validate computational claims made in scientific machine learning papers. This workflow treats each claim as a target with recorded evidence, guiding the agent to reconstruct methods, run experiments, and verify outputs against the original claims before completing the replication process. The approach was tested on twelve independent runs across four papers, successfully matching all recorded targets with corresponding evidence in the replication reports. The Paper-replication workflow ensures that completion depends on validated workspace evidence rather than the agent's final message, addressing challenges in preserving progress and verifying generated evidence. Despite consistent completion, repeated runs showed variability in how papers were divided into targets, numerical fidelity, replication time, and evidence acceptance criteria, highlighting the complexity of replicating scientific machine learning results.

entry.title: Researchers present A2utoLPBench, an auto-generated linear programming benchmark with known optimal solutions for testing LLM-driven agents, offering unlimited fresh problems and resistance to training data leakage [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced A²utoLPBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate large language model (LLM)-driven agents on linear programming problems presented in plain text. Unlike traditional static datasets, A²utoLPBench generates problems automatically by selecting feasible points and duals to construct linear programs with known optimal solutions, eliminating the need for solvers or human annotation. This approach provides an unlimited supply of fresh problems with adjustable difficulty, ensuring accurate ground-truth answers and reducing the risk of training data leakage.
